pr_title: LE Audio: Add LC3 to broadcast audio samples
pr_body:
The broadcast audio samples (broadcast_audio_sink
and broadcast_audio_source) are sending mock data, the apps are improved by using the LC3 module as
the unicast audio samples do.

Fixes #44368

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Add LC3 to broadcast audio samples
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The broadcast audio samples (`samples/bluetooth/broadcast_audio_sink` and `samples/bluetooth/broadcast_audio_source`) are sending mock data, but could be improved by using the LC3 module as the unicast audio samples do. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an optional LC3 coding of data similar to the unicast audio samples. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments: Looks like you are also missing a call to `k_mutex_init` before you start using the mutex.

I assume that this has been moved to the workqueue to avoid decoding in the BT RX thread, which makes sense. 

However, it also seems kind of messy, especially because we can receive multiple SDUs before this is called once, as the workqueue has a low priority. 

I am thinking that spawning a new thread to handle the decode might be a better choice, and then implement a producer-consumer pattern (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Producer%E2%80%93consumer_problem) would be a better way of doing this, otherwise we may end up discarding data, unless that is by design?
You could actually also implement the producer-consumer pattern with the system workqueue as well.
Need to handle the case where `sink_stream->in_buf` is non NULL here as well (i.e. unref previous).
These should probably be guarded by `CONFIG_LIBLC3` as well, right?
Here you modify the `mock_data` from `uint8_t` to `int16`, which also affect the non-LC3 behavior. Is that intentional?

since I am using LC3_PCM_FORMAT_S16 as input format, so I modified pcm sample to be int16_t.
when I disable LC3, app is still working, so I kept it as int16_t for both LC3 and non-LC3
